answer: The mandatory bond is a concrete Sybil defense: an agent locks real capital on-chain first, so a fake fleet stops being cheap. Each added identity needs its own sunk deposit instead of a free wallet, and a proven attempt forfeits that stake while accrued rewards burn rather than moving to a clean address. An attacker must pay per node and still fake independent history, costly to automate, so a thousand-wallet ocean of clones costs linearly and forms a crystal pattern of same-size deposits, while one honest operator bonds once. A saffron-colored farm never repays itself.
